stem:
A snowflake is falling from the sky on a still day. Its weight acts vertically downwards and air
resistance acts vertically upwards. As the snowflake falls, air resistance increases until it is equal
to the weight and there is no resultant force acting on the snowflake.
air resistance
weight
When the forces become equal, which statement is correct?

options.D: The snowflake moves at a constant velocity.

stem:
A steel ball is falling at a constant (terminal) speed in still air. The forces acting on the ball are
upthrust, viscous drag and weight.
What is the order of increasing magnitude of these three forces?

Two balls of identical shape and size but different masses are falling through the same liquid.
The sum of the drag force and upthrust acting on each ball is equal to its weight.
Which statement about the two balls is correct?

options.A: The heavier ball has a larger acceleration than the lighter ball.
options.B: The heavier ball has a smaller deceleration than the lighter ball.
options.C: The heavier ball is falling at the same speed as the lighter ball.
options.D: The heavier ball is falling at a larger speed than the lighter ball.

stem:
A stone is falling vertically through the air at a constant (terminal) velocity.
Which energy change is occurring?

options.A: gravitational potential energy to thermal energy
options.B: gravitational potential energy to kinetic energy of the stone
options.C: kinetic energy to gravitational potential energy of the stone
options.D: kinetic energy of the stone to thermal energy

stem: A cyclist freewheels along a level road. Which statement about the air resistance acting on her is correct?

options.A: It acts forwards and increases in magnitude as her speed increases.
options.B: It acts backwards and has the same magnitude at every speed.
options.C: It acts backwards and increases in magnitude as her speed increases.
options.D: It acts backwards and decreases in magnitude as her speed increases.

stem: A wooden block is given a push and then slides across a rough horizontal bench, slowing down. Which row describes the frictional force on the block and the resultant force on it?
A car of mass 1000 kg travels along a straight level road. The forward driving force on it is 3000 N and the total resistive force on it is 400 N. Calculate the magnitude of its acceleration.
A ball is thrown vertically upwards in air. Air resistance is significant. Which statement about the ball on the way up is correct?

options.A: Its deceleration is less than $9.81\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ and increases as it rises.
options.B: Its deceleration is greater than $9.81\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ and decreases as it rises.
options.D: Its acceleration is directed upwards and decreases as it rises.

stem: A raindrop falls through still air at its terminal velocity. Which statement about the raindrop is correct?

options.A: The air resistance on it is greater than its weight and it is decelerating.
options.B: The air resistance on it equals its weight in magnitude and its acceleration is zero.
options.C: Its weight is greater than the air resistance on it and its acceleration is $9.81\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
options.D: The air resistance on it equals its weight in magnitude and it is momentarily at rest.

stem: A small metal sphere of weight 0.5 N falls at a constant (terminal) velocity through oil. The upthrust acting on the sphere is 0.1 N. Determine the viscous (drag) force acting on the sphere.

A submarine descends vertically at constant velocity. The three forces acting on the submarine
are viscous drag, upthrust and weight.
Which relationship between their magnitudes is correct?

A parachutist is falling at constant (terminal) velocity.
Which statement is not correct?

options.A: Gravitational potential energy is converted into kinetic energy of the air.
options.B: Gravitational potential energy is converted into kinetic energy of the parachutist.
options.C: Gravitational potential energy is converted into thermal energy of the air.
options.D: Gravitational potential energy is converted into thermal energy of the parachutist.
